headline: Democrats swept the midterms and AI data-centre stocks wobbled, but the semis ETF bounced 2.0% and grid (+5.4%, Primoris +15.1% on five days) kept leading while the ETF stays -18.2% on the month.
regime: Nasdaq +0.8% and the semis ETF +2.0% on the day, but -4.2% and -7.1% on five days and -7.7% and -18.2% on the month; VIX eased 12.3% to 18.26. The 10-year is 4.95% and crude $95.15 (+6.4% on the month). Grid is the only segment up on five days (+5.8%); software (-16.8%), compute (-12.4%) and optical (-12.1%) are weakest. Policy risk to data-centre build-outs is the new variable, yet company prints (Eaton, Primoris, Super Micro, Astera) are strong: fundamentals and prices still disagree.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Eaton: record $20bn backlog, beat the high end of guidance on every metric, data-centre demand up 65% (caeb9a06e4c3)
Primoris surged on an earnings beat and strong guidance; grid +5.8% on five days (647e624dd52c)
Talen: adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled, 2027 targets above 25% growth, $3bn buyback (9164a217b18a)
Against: Eaton fell 16% in a month and Vertiv and GE Vernova fell with it (07170387f5de); Modine missed EPS by 12.9% (8d8a52205d05)
theses.change_note: +1: more record backlog and a grid rally into a sweep that threatens data-centre policy; Modine's miss and the monthly drops cap the gain.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Super Micro revenue $19.9bn, up 298% year on year; one AI order can exceed a year-ago quarter (206a15f03f0e, 5a7860879472)
Astera Labs revenue $584.9m, up 154% (5ab9466a1684)
AMD's Lisa Su eyes 80% growth in 2027 (584a6fd9677e)
Against: compute -23% and foundry equipment -28.5% on the month (digest segments); Astera's inventory tripled (e87b2be56b85)
theses.change_note: +4: three huge prints and guidance in one day; the price action still says the market doubts duration, so no more than that.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: DigitalOcean -36% and TeraWulf -20% in a month on build-out funding fears (b995b2f7ee6a, 1c65fd13e1c8)
CoreWeave fair value trimmed as analysts split on financing risk (ab7f6e4b413c)
Against: the group rose 9.6% on the day, Oracle's $20bn raise showed lenders still lend (04faf04aa5bf), TeraWulf upsized its credit line (995568815f73)
theses.change_note: -1: a violent relief bounce and open credit markets; the group is still -24.3% on the month and fails the cash-flow gate.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: A NAND maker with 84.6% margins is down 51% from its high (106f7866dc9d)
ETFs bought $262.9m of Micron on Nov. 2 (4bdd8ca96c9e)
Against: memory -9.9% on five days and -26.6% on the month, Micron the best at -7.9% (digest segments)
Against: Astera's tripled inventory repeats the stocking-ahead signal (e87b2be56b85)
theses.change_note: -2: no new fundamental news and the group is still falling on five days; margin-versus-price gap is the only support.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Oracle priced a $20bn stock and bond sale to fund AI (04faf04aa5bf)
Google is expanding voluntary exit packages to five more countries, a cost-cutting sign (5ed7437d8f5b)
Against: Jassy's message points to AI-driven AWS revenue growth (a4a1b9053861)
theses.change_note: -2: Oracle's raise was well received and AWS growth offsets; no new cash-flow data.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Semis ETF -18.2% and Nasdaq -7.7% on the month, 10-year 4.95% (digest tape)
AI infrastructure meets the 5% Treasury yield test (7146e5110179)
Against: VIX fell 12.3% on the day, and post-midterm seasonality is cited as supportive (97c15473628e)
theses.change_note: -2: a calmer VIX and a bounce, but the 10-year is at 4.95% and every group is still deeply negative on the month.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: AI data-centre stocks dropped as Democrats swept the midterms (3c75d0cd7417)
Texas paused its data-centre boom (99ff96f5fbd2)
Against: futures reversed higher and AMD and Arista rallied after the sweep (5e4f41f72dd8)
theses.change_note: New and low-confidence: the sell-off reversed within hours, so the market is treating it as headline risk until legislation appears.

compute.note: -12.4% on five days, Marvell -29.4%; AMD and Astera prints are strong but price trend is down.

foundry_equipment.note: -28.5% on the month; KLA +1.7% on five days, Teradyne -16.8%; buy only quality.

memory_storage.note: -26.6% on the month; margins are high but buyers may be stocking.

networking_optical.note: -31% on the month; Fabrinet and Astera beat, Lumentum -21.5% on five days.

servers.note: Super Micro record $19.9bn quarter, but Dell -18.6% on five days.

power_nuclear.note: Talen EBITDA nearly doubled with a $3bn buyback; developers like Oklo still burn cash.

grid_electrical.note: Only segment up on five days (+5.8%); Eaton record backlog, Primoris +15.1%.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv +13.1% on five days; Modine missed EPS and Trane -9.5%.

datacenter_neocloud.note: +9.6% bounce is not a thesis change; funding stress and the cash-flow gate remain.

hyperscalers.note: Oracle's $20bn raise; Alphabet -12.7% on five days; policy risk adds.

risks: Democratic control of Congress could bring data-centre scrutiny that delays orders for power and cooling suppliers.
The 10-year at 4.95% is on the edge of 5%, which would compress multiples further.
Oil near $95-104 on Middle East tensions and the Iran war keeps inflation and rates sticky.
Inventory tripling at Astera and Dell could mean stocking ahead of an order slowdown.
Neocloud funding stress could hit GPU, power and cooling orders if lenders close.
watch: Whether grid and cooling hold up if the post-midterm bounce fades.
Any concrete data-centre legislation or state moratoria after Texas.
The 10-year against 5% and the semis ETF against -20% on the month.
Camtek earnings today and Powell Industries' fiscal Q4 date.
Ciena's next report for whether margins keep up with 37% growth.
